authoritative_representation.decision: timestamps = naive UTC; business dates = calendar `Date`; durations = hours from HH:MM rows

tz_assumptions.tz_aware_arithmetic: none in production paths (`astimezone` 1 site, `timezone.utc` 13 sites, all in _now_utc/packaging)
tz_assumptions.storage: tzinfo deliberately stripped for SQLite compatibility (documented in the _now_utc docstring)
tz_assumptions.display: 49 `datetime.now()` sites, all display/filename/report-stamp only (footer text, export filenames, status bar, audit_id string); no persistence column is fed local time
tz_assumptions.dst: not modelled: no tz-aware conversions; wall-clock HH:MM + local calendar dates. A DST transition cannot corrupt stored durations because durations are row values, not computed from timestamps

duration_semantics.contract: unknown/invalid duration never becomes 0 and never completes a denominator; no rows => None; recorded 0 stays 0; NULL is_npt cannot prove productive time

date_boundary_and_operational_day.concept: 24:00 is a legal end-of-day value (operational day = 00:00..24:00)
evidence: core/time_utils.py — TimeLineEdit/TimeValidator accept 24:00 and expose is_midnight_24
core/import_quality.py:621-625 — 24h coverage check requires a midnight start and end
core/ddr_pdf_export.py:104 — DDR renders 00:00 vs 06:00 depth columns
date_boundary_and_operational_day.day_boundary: report_date is a Date column (00:00-24:00 local day); no shift-start offset is applied

serialization.db: SQLAlchemy DateTime/Date -> SQLite TEXT/ISO by default
serialization.export: isoformat()/strftime used at display boundaries only
serialization.json_payload: core/data_quality.py:273 evidence.timestamp uses local naive isoformat in a returned payload (not persisted); a convention inconsistency with the UTC storage rule, recorded as an observation, behaviour unchanged
